propositions.name: quantity_of_matter_from_density_and_bulk
propositions.statement: The quantity of matter arises from its density and bulk conjunctly.
propositions.quote: The quantity of matter is the measure of the same, arising from its density and bulk conjunctly.

propositions.name: mass_proportional_to_weight
propositions.statement: The quantity of matter of a body is proportional to its weight, as found by experiments on pendulums.
propositions.quote: for it is proportional to the weight, as I have found by experiments on pendulums, very accurately made

propositions.name: quantity_of_motion_from_velocity_and_matter
propositions.statement: The quantity of motion arises from the velocity and quantity of matter conjunctly.
propositions.quote: The quantity of motion is the measure of the same, arising from the velocity and quantity of matter conjunctly.

propositions.name: motion_of_whole_is_sum_of_parts
propositions.statement: The motion of the whole is the sum of the motions of all the parts.
propositions.quote: The motion of the whole is the sum of the motions of all the parts

propositions.name: bodies_persevere_in_state
propositions.statement: Every body endeavours to persevere in its present state, whether of rest or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.
propositions.quote: every body, as much as in it lies, endeavours to persevere in its present state, whether it be of rest, or of moving uniformly forward in a right line

propositions.name: vis_insita_proportional_to_body
propositions.statement: The vis insita is ever proportional to the body whose force it is and differs nothing from the inactivity of the mass.
propositions.quote: This force is ever proportional to the body whose force it is; and differs nothing from the inactivity of the mass, but in our manner of conceiving it

propositions.name: impressed_force_is_action
propositions.statement: An impressed force is an action exerted upon a body in order to change its state of rest or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.
propositions.quote: An impressed force is an action exerted upon a body, in order to change its state, either of rest, or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.

propositions.name: impressed_force_remains_no_longer
propositions.statement: An impressed force consists in the action only and remains no longer in the body when the action is over.
propositions.quote: This force consists in the action only; and remains no longer in the body, when the action is over.

propositions.name: impressed_force_origins
propositions.statement: Impressed forces are of different origins as from percussion, from pressure, and from centripetal force.
propositions.quote: Impressed forces are of different origins as from percussion, from pressure, from centripetal force.

propositions.name: gravity_toward_earth_centre
propositions.statement: Gravity is a centripetal force by which bodies tend to the centre of the earth.
propositions.quote: Of this sort is gravity, by which bodies tend to the centre of the earth

propositions.name: magnetism_iron_to_loadstone
propositions.statement: Magnetism is a centripetal force by which iron tends to the loadstone.
propositions.quote: magnetism, by which iron tends to the loadstone; and that force, what ever it is, by which the planets are perpetually drawn aside from the rectilinear motions

propositions.name: planets_drawn_from_rectilinear
propositions.statement: The planets are perpetually drawn aside from the rectilinear motions they would otherwise pursue and made to revolve in curvilinear orbits.
propositions.quote: the planets are perpetually drawn aside from the rectilinear motions, which otherwise they would pursue, and made to revolve in curvilinear orbits

propositions.name: orbiting_bodies_endeavour_to_recede
propositions.statement: All bodies revolved in orbits endeavour to recede from the centres of their orbits and, without a contrary centripetal force, would fly off in right lines with uniform motion.
propositions.quote: They all endeavour to recede from the centres of their orbits; and were it not for the opposition of a contrary force which restrains them to, and detains them in their orbits, which I therefore call centripetal

propositions.name: projectile_without_gravity_goes_straight
propositions.statement: A projectile, if not for the force of gravity, would not deviate towards the earth but would go off in a right line with uniform motion if the resistance of the air was taken away.
propositions.quote: A projectile, if it was not for the force of gravity, would not deviate towards the earth, but would go off from it in a right line, and that with an uniform motion

propositions.name: moon_needs_force_to_orbit
propositions.statement: The moon could not be retained in its orbit without some force drawing it aside from a rectilinear way.
propositions.quote: nor could the moon with out some such force, be retained in its orbit

propositions.name: gravity_stronger_near_earth
propositions.statement: The force of gravity is greater in valleys, less on tops of exceeding high mountains, and yet less at greater distances from the body of the earth.
propositions.quote: the force of gravity is greater in valleys, less on tops of exceeding high mountains; and yet less (as shall hereafter be shown), at greater distances from the body of the earth

propositions.name: gravity_accelerates_all_bodies_equally
propositions.statement: At equal distances gravity equally accelerates all falling bodies, whether heavy or light, great or small.
propositions.quote: it equally accelerates all falling bodies, whether heavy or light, great or small

propositions.name: weight_varies_with_distance_from_earth
propositions.statement: In the same body the weight is greater near to the earth and less at remoter distances.
propositions.quote: in the same body, it is greater near to the earth, and less at remoter distances

propositions.name: motive_force_from_accelerative_and_matter
propositions.statement: The motive force arises from the accelerative force drawn into the same quantity of matter.
propositions.quote: the motive force arises from the accelerative force drawn into the same quantity of matter

propositions.name: absolute_time_flows_equably
propositions.statement: Absolute, true, and mathematical time, of itself and from its own nature, flows equably without regard to anything external.
propositions.quote: Absolute, true, and mathematical time, of itself, and from its own nature flows equably without regard to anything external, and by another name is called duration

propositions.name: absolute_space_immovable
propositions.statement: Absolute space, in its own nature, without regard to anything external, remains always similar and immovable.
propositions.quote: Absolute space, in its own nature, without regard to anything external, remains always similar and immovable

propositions.name: natural_days_truly_unequal
propositions.statement: The natural days are truly unequal, though they are commonly considered as equal and used for a measure of time.
propositions.quote: For the natural days are truly unequal, though they are commonly considered as equal, and used for a measure of time

propositions.name: maybe_no_equable_motion_for_time
propositions.statement: It may be that there is no such thing as an equable motion whereby time may be accurately measured.
propositions.quote: It may be, that there is no such thing as an equable motion, whereby time may be accurately measured

propositions.name: absolute_time_liable_to_no_change
propositions.statement: All motions may be accelerated and retarded, but the true or equable progress of absolute time is liable to no change.
propositions.quote: All motions may be accelerated and retarded, but the true, or equable, progress of absolute time is liable to no change

propositions.name: order_of_time_and_space_immutable
propositions.statement: The order of the parts of time is immutable, so also is the order of the parts of space.
propositions.quote: As the order of the parts of time is immutable, so also is the order of the parts of space

propositions.name: parts_of_space_not_sensible
propositions.statement: The parts of space cannot be seen or distinguished from one another by our senses.
propositions.quote: the parts of space cannot be seen, or distinguished from one another by our senses

propositions.name: maybe_no_body_really_at_rest
propositions.statement: It may be that there is no body really at rest to which the places and motions of others may be referred.
propositions.quote: For it may be that there is no body really at rest, to which the places and motions of others may be referred

propositions.name: bodies_at_rest_rest_together
propositions.statement: It is a property of rest that bodies really at rest do rest in respect to one another.
propositions.quote: It is a property of rest, that bodies really at rest do rest in respect to one another

propositions.name: body_absolutely_at_rest_beyond_stars
propositions.statement: In the remote regions of the fixed stars, or perhaps far beyond them, there may be some body absolutely at rest.
propositions.quote: in the remote regions of the fixed stars, or perhaps far beyond them, there may be some body absolutely at rest

propositions.name: absolute_rest_undetermined_locally
propositions.statement: Absolute rest cannot be determined from the position of bodies in our regions.
propositions.quote: it follows that absolute rest cannot be determined from the position of bodies in our regions

propositions.name: parts_partake_of_wholes_motion
propositions.statement: The parts which retain given positions to their wholes do partake of the motions of those wholes.
propositions.quote: the parts, which retain given positions to their wholes, do partake of the motions of those wholes

propositions.name: revolving_parts_recede_from_axis
propositions.statement: All the parts of revolving bodies endeavour to recede from the axis of motion.
propositions.quote: all the parts of revolving bodies endeavour to recede from the axis of motion

propositions.name: true_motion_requires_impressed_force
propositions.statement: True motion is neither generated nor altered but by some force impressed upon the body moved.
propositions.quote: True motion is neither generated nor altered, but by some force impressed upon the body moved

propositions.name: relative_motion_without_impressed_force
propositions.statement: Relative motion may be generated or altered without any force impressed upon the body.
propositions.quote: relative motion may be generated or altered without any force impressed upon the body

propositions.name: circular_motion_recedes_from_axis
propositions.statement: The effects which distinguish absolute from relative motion are the forces of receding from the axis of circular motion.
propositions.quote: The effects which distinguish absolute from relative motion are, the forces of receding from the axis of circular motion

propositions.name: water_in_vessel_forms_concave
propositions.statement: Water in a whirled vessel begins to revolve, recedes from the middle, and ascends to the sides of the vessel, forming itself into a concave figure.
propositions.quote: will make it begin sensibly to revolve, and recede by little and little from the middle, and ascend to the sides of the vessel, forming itself into a concave figure

propositions.name: one_true_circular_motion_per_body
propositions.statement: There is only one real circular motion of any one revolving body, corresponding to only one power of endeavouring to recede from its axis of motion.
propositions.quote: There is only one real circular motion of any one revolving body, corresponding to only one power of endeavouring to recede from its axis of motion

propositions.name: two_globes_cord_tension_reveals_motion
propositions.statement: From the tension of a cord connecting two revolved globes we might discover the endeavour of the globes to recede from the axis of their motion.
propositions.quote: we might, from the tension of the cord, discover the endeavour of the globes to recede from the axis of their motion

propositions.name: fixed_stars_keep_positions
propositions.statement: The fixed stars in our regions keep always a given position one to another.
propositions.quote: some remote bodies were placed that kept always a given position one to another, as the fixed stars do in our regions

propositions.name: pendulum_and_jupiter_satellites_evince_equation
propositions.statement: The necessity of the equation for determining the times of a phenomenon is evinced from the experiments of the pendulum clock and by eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter.
propositions.quote: The necessity of which equation, for determining the times of a phenomenon, is evinced as well from the experiments of the pendulum clock, as by eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter
